questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A place with courses in English + a place with relevant courses + a nice country

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: From University of Trento there is a nice guide for exchange students. I had more problems before arrival with KU and trying to work out deadlines with slow email responses, not a correct sign-up and unclear information about the learning agreement.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The University of Trento has a good ESN-organisation with information about living in Italy. Plus we had an orientation session at the university with practical information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was lucky and had connections to Trento through a Danish friend. Other erasmus students found accommodation on Facebook.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's nice to live in the city center or around the center of Trento. Even when studying in Rovereto, it's better to live in Trento to be able to meet people at all the events.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You just put the courses in your Online learning agreement. You don't sign up any other way. And you have two weeks to make your decision, so it's also possible to attend some courses and then change your mind.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: E-mail correspondence with the international office.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I could go to all the classes I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try out a lot of courses in the beginning, so you know better what you want. Read online about the exams for every courses (There's a difference between attending and non-attending students)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were not that difficult compared to the level at KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In Trento, you had to do a lot of presentations before being able to write the final essay for the exam. At KU, you only need to write the exam (usually).

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Civil Societies and Contentious Politics,
Corso di italiano A1a - II periodo (intensivo),
International Economics (Basic),
Labour Rights in the Global Economy,
Party Politics and Democracy in Europe,
Sociology of collective action

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The italian course is nice to get knowledge about Italy and a basic understanding of the language. I liked Party Politics and Democracy in Europe as well because the subject was very political-science. The Civil Societies and Contentious Politics-course had a nice, engaged teacher, I can recommend that as well.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The phone bill was a bit higher than expected, but I stayed with my Danish company. Would have been cheaper to buy an Italian simcard.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Eating/drinking out is very cheap compared to Denmark.
Groceries are not that different from Denmark

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very expensive to sign up for the UniTrento sport + a lot in Italian

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: UniTrentoSport, Erasmus Student Network, other free open events.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Events organised by Erasmus Student Network (ESN) in order to get to know a lot of people.
If you want to get to know more italian students, go to Bruno.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Hiking! Go to the mountains all around the area
A lot of small, nice museums to discover as well
Trento is an easy link to take the train to other Italian regions.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The food culture is different (eating later for example), but not that hard to adjust to.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Play a sports. You can go for free to beach volley courts and play with italians.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Eating later. Living slow (slower walking, slow in the supermarket, trains/busses are almost always late). But it's okay to work with.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Italians being very friendly and open to speak. The delicious food.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Go to the events with other Erasmus-students to make friends. Go on hikes in the mountains. Find housing in the city center.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Exam sessions are usually in June, July and September. You can choose yourself which of the dates to attend. And if you don't like your grade from the first exam, you can reject the grade and try again the next date of exam.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living on my own in a new country, creating "a life" from scratch - and then finding out it's not so bad to be by yourself, because it forces you to try new activities and talk to new people. My new friends are what is most rewarding.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To leave home for the unknown.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I can only recommend others to go on exchange. Especially in Trento. Here you have the perfect combination of doing outdoor sports like hiking, climbing, biking, swimming and skiing; while still enjoying the lakes during the summer, going for drinks at bars and eating pizza with your friends. The city is small, so meeting friends around the corner is the best. And also that everyone lives close, so "meet me at the duomo" is the classic starting point.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
